Exterior establishing plate for a historical docudrama — a tiny flat tropical island launch site in the Pacific at dawn, September 2008: a slim white two-stage orbital rocket about 21 meters tall standing upright on a small concrete pad, black "SPACEX" lettering down its side, a single lattice lightning mast beside it, low palm scrub, and the ocean stretching to the horizon on every side — the smallness of the island must read clearly. Golden-pink dawn sky, teal ocean, the rocket rim-lit by the rising sun. Vertical 9:16-friendly composition. RAW 35mm Kodak Portra 400 color, real shadow falloff, real material texture, believable physical detail everywhere. NOT a 3D render, NOT smoothed, NOT an AI-CGI look — a real photographed location, muted unpolished documentary grade, photojournalism feel. No people anywhere in frame.
